name: Contaminated stormwater collection and diversion
principle: Refinery and petrochemical sites segregate clean and contaminated stormwater. IPIECA: contaminated stormwater must be collected separately and stored until it can be treated in the wastewater treatment plant; the first-flush volume — the first one to two inches of rain — is captured in a tank or basin and discharged to wastewater treatment at a controlled rate.

process_steps.name: Controlled treatment feed
equipment: pumps to the ETP at a controlled rate

performance.basis: the first one to two inches of rain captured (IPIECA)

source.note: IPIECA Refining Water Best Practices (mirrored PDF), read 2026-11-18

sources.note: IPIECA Refining Water Best Practices (mirrored PDF), read 2026-11-18

advantages: Keeps hydrocarbon-contaminated runoff out of untreated discharge
Uses existing ETP capacity instead of a dedicated plant
limitations: Basin sizing is site- and rainfall-specific
Beyond first flush, flows may bypass treatment — site water-balance discipline required
